skill.name: iotnet
skill.description: IoT network traffic analyzer for detecting IoT protocols and identifying security vulnerabilities in packet captures or authorized live traffic.
skill.summary: Analyze IoT packet captures and authorized live traffic for protocol use and security weaknesses.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline option names. The sudo examples and live-capture note are confirmed high-risk findings because the skill asks agents to perform packet capture with elevated privileges. The sample private IP address and IP filter option are documentation examples, not hostile network reconnaissance.

remediation.issue: Privileged live network capture is documented with sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user authorization before live capture and prefer least-privilege packet capture setup over broad sudo execution.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be run without enough safety context.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to verify the interface, duration, filter, and authorization before executing any live capture command.

remediation.issue: Packet captures can contain credentials, device identifiers, and personal traffic.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to protect PCAP files, redact sensitive output, and avoid sharing raw captures outside approved environments.

static_findings.snippet: - `pcap_files`: One or more PCAP files to analyze
- `-c, --capture-filter`: BPF syntax filter for live capture
- `--display-filter`: Wireshark display filter for PCAP analysis
- `--config`: Custom IoT detection rules configuration file

content.value_statement: IoT teams need clear evidence from packet captures and live traffic. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through IoT protocol and vulnerability analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guide offline analysis of one or more PCAP files with iotnet.
Guide live traffic capture on a selected network interface.
Apply IP, BPF, and Wireshark display filters to focus analysis.
Identify IoT protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, Z-Wave, ONVIF, UPnP, and Modbus.
Summarize vulnerabilities such as missing encryption, weak authentication, and plaintext credentials.
Use custom detection rule files for organization-specific checks.
limitations: Live capture requires authorized access to the network interface and elevated privileges.
The skill does not include the iotnet binary or detection rule files.
Results depend on packet capture quality and available protocol metadata.
It cannot prove device compromise without supporting evidence.

use_cases.title: Audit Lab Capture
use_cases.description: Review captured device traffic to identify insecure protocols, missing encryption, and weak authentication before deployment.

use_cases.title: Triage Field Network
use_cases.description: Capture a short authorized traffic sample from a selected interface and summarize device communication risks.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Produce clear findings and remediation notes from PCAP files for client reports.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a PCAP
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the PCAP at [path]. Report detected IoT protocols, vulnerabilities, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on One Device
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [path] for device [IP address]. Separate normal communication from risky plaintext or weak authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Authorized Traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture authorized traffic on [interface] for [duration] seconds. Use safe filters and summarize IoT security issues.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Rules and Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [PCAP paths] with [custom rules file] and [display filter]. Prioritize high severity findings and evidence for remediation.

output_examples.input: Analyze a packet capture from a smart thermostat lab.
output_examples.output: The report identifies MQTT and SSDP traffic, notes missing TLS, and recommends enabling encryption and stronger authentication.

output_examples.input: Review traffic from a single camera IP address.
output_examples.output: The output groups ONVIF and RTSP traffic, flags plaintext credentials, and lists packets that need manual confirmation.

output_examples.input: Summarize authorized live capture from a test VLAN.
output_examples.output: The summary lists protocol counts, suspicious device behavior, and a prioritized remediation checklist.

best_practices: Use this skill only on networks and packet captures you are authorized to analyze.
Prefer offline PCAP analysis when live capture is not required.
Record filters, capture duration, and rule files with every finding.
anti_patterns: Do not run live capture on networks without explicit permission.
Do not treat sample IP addresses or commands as production policy.
Do not publish packet data that may contain credentials or personal information.

faq.question: Does this skill install iotnet?
faq.answer: No. It describes how to use the existing iotnet command from iothackbot.

faq.question: Can it analyze live traffic?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user provides an authorized interface and duration. Live capture may require elevated privileges.

faq.question: Can it analyze PCAP files?
faq.answer: Yes. PCAP analysis is the safer default and does not require live network access.

faq.question: Which protocols can it identify?
faq.answer: It can guide analysis for MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, Z-Wave, ONVIF, UPnP, Modbus, and configurable protocols.

faq.question: Does it replace manual security review?
faq.answer: No. It organizes findings and recommendations, but analysts should validate important evidence.

faq.question: Why is elevated privilege mentioned?
faq.answer: Packet capture tools often need access to raw network interfaces. Use the least privilege method available.
